Seminal

/SEM-uh-nl/ - the stress falls on SEM · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Seminal means original and important; creating a field.

Choreographers still mine the 1972 kung-fu picture; its wire-work made it seminal for the whole genre.

Worked Example

In 1978 a Florida teenager popped his skateboard off flat ground — no ramp, no hands — and landed with the board still under his feet. Every kickflip, every stair trick, every contest run since descends from that one motion. Skaters call the ollie seminal and mean it root and all: the seed the whole modern vocabulary grew from.

Seminal makes a claim fame can't: descent. Plenty of famous tricks were dead ends — admired, replayed, never built upon. The root is semin-, seed: a seminal work is one later work grows from. If nothing grew from it, it may be brilliant, but it isn't seminal.

How Seminal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

groundbreaking

groundbreaking: first to do it — with or without descendants

foundational

foundational: what the later structure visibly stands on

Antonyms

derivative

derivative: grown from someone else's seed

imitative

imitative: copying the manner of others

How Strong Is It? — admired → groundbreaking → seminal

admired vs. seminal

admired vs. seminal: Admired work wins the evening; it may still change nothing. Seminal work is still being answered decades later.

groundbreaking vs. seminal

groundbreaking vs. seminal: Groundbreaking means nobody had done it before; seminal asks the harder question — did everybody after do it because of you?

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — semin-

Root — semin-: seed (Latin semen, seminis)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Semin- (seed — Latin semen, seminis) + -al (relating to) = of the nature of a seed. Romans used the root for actual sowing; English planted it in the library: a seminal paper, album, or design is the seed a field grows from — and you can trace the field's rings back to it.

Use the root in a new word: seminar

Use the root in a new word: seminar: The honors seminar meets around one table, a dozen students growing arguments from a single text.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / academic

Seminal is the historian's word, awarded with hindsight: from this seed, the field. Groundbreaking (its own synonym chip) honors a first; seminal requires descendants — call nothing seminal until you can name what grew from it. Reserve it for the founding paper, album, or design, not merely the best one.
